sentences.text: Something about this peaceful sleeping woman feels completely wrong, filled with hidden dread.
This is The Nightmare, painted by Henry Fuseli in 1781.
A glowing woman lies draped over a bed, resting peacefully in dark surroundings.
According to art critic Nicholas Powell, the crouching demon derives from ancient sculptures at Selinunte.
The sleeper should have woken up.
But a heavy weight kept her completely paralyzed.
The woman appears peacefully asleep, yet a demonic weight presses upon her.
As if her bad dream took physical shape upon her body.
So is that heavy feeling on your chest just a dream?

sources.claim: The Nightmare is a 1781 oil painting by the Swiss artist Henry Fuseli.

It shows a woman with her arms thrown below her, in deep sleep as she undergoes a nightmare as an almost hidden horse (the "night-mare") looks on as a demonic and ape-like incubus crouches on her ches

It shows a woman with her arms thrown below her, in deep sleep as she undergoes a nightmare as an almost hidden horse (the "night-mare") looks on as a demonic and ape-like incubus crouches on her ches
She is mounted by an incubus that peers out at the viewer.

She is mounted by an incubus that peers out at the viewer.
According to the art critic Nicholas Powell, the woman's pose may derive from the Vatican's Ariadne, and the style of the incubus from figures at Selinunte, an archaeological site in Sicily.
The early meaning of nightmare included the sleeper's experience of weight on the chest combined with sleep paralysis, dyspnea, or a feeling of dread.
Description The Nightmare simultaneously offers both the image of a dream—by indicating the effect of the nightmare on the woman—and a dream image—in symbolically portraying the sleeping vision.
